title: Lung ultrasound-guided protocolized fluid management versus conventional central venous pressure-based management in monitoring extravascular lung water during the perioperative period of percutaneous nephrolithotomy: a randomized controlled trial

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Lung ultrasound-guided protocolized fluid management versus conventional central venous pressure-based management in monitoring extravascular lung water during the perioperative period of percutaneous nephrolithotomy: a randomized controlled trial》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · S0001-p1】As a minimally invasive surgery, percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) has been frequently used for managing renal calculi [1]. To ensure a clear surgical field, irrigation fluid is required to irrigate the stone sites, such as the renal pelvis and calyces [2]. However, excessive absorption of irrigation fluid enhances the body’s fluid load, thereby raising the hydrostatic pressure in the alveolar capillaries and promoting the production of extravascular lung water (EVLW) [3]. This might induce pulmonary edema and even lead to heart failure, worsening the patient’s condition. Therefore, anesthesiologists should promptly identify and address the potential adverse effects of increased perioperative EVLW on various body systems to ensure the patient’s intraoperative anesthesia safety. Hence, the objective monitoring, accurate prediction, and assessment of the body’s volume status are critical in clinical anesthesia practice.

【Introduction · S0001-p4】Consequently, this study aimed to evaluate a protocolized fluid management strategy guided by LUS, in which predefined ECS thresholds trigger early intervention, and compare it with conventional CVP-based management during PCNL. We hypothesized that integrating LUS’s superior sensitivity for EVLW detection with a structured intervention protocol would improve perioperative outcomes compared with reactive management based on CVP thresholds and clinical judgment.

However, excessive absorption of irrigation fluid enhances the body’s fluid load, thereby raising the hydrostatic pressure in the alveolar capillaries and promoting the production of extravascular lung water (EVLW) [3]. This might induce pulmonary edema and even lead to heart failure, worsening the patient’s condition. Therefore, anesthesiologists should promptly identify and address the potential adverse effects of increased perioperative EVLW on various body systems to ensure the patient’s intraoperative anesthesia safety. Hence, the objective monitoring, accurate prediction, and assessment of the body’s volume status are critical in clinical anesthesia practice.

Consequently, this study aimed to evaluate a protocolized fluid management strategy guided by LUS, in which predefined ECS thresholds trigger early intervention, and compare it with conventional CVP-based management during PCNL. We hypothesized that integrating LUS’s superior sensitivity for EVLW detection with a structured intervention protocol would improve perioperative outcomes compared with reactive management based on CVP thresholds and clinical judgment.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Lung ultrasound-guided protocolized fluid management versus conventional central venous pressure-based management in monitoring extravascular lung water during the perioperative period of percutaneous nephrolithotomy: a randomized controlled trial》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Patient enrolment · S0002-S2001-p1】The Ethics Committee of Second Affiliated Hospital of Zunyi Medical University approved our study protocol (KYLL-2022-057). This study was registered at the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry on September 5, 2023 (Registration Number: ChiCTR2300075416). URL: https: www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=201155. Patient enrollment commenced on October 10, 2023. Written informed consent was obtained from all participating subjects; for subjects unable to provide consent independently, informed consent was signed by their corresponding family members or legal representatives.

【Patient enrolment · S0002-S2001-p2】After pre-trial preparations from September to October 2023, we enrolled 181 patients undergoing elective PCNL at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Zunyi Medical University between October 2023 and December 2024. Our inclusion criteria included: patients aged >18 years; those with Body Mass Index (BMI) of 18.5–28 kg/m2; participants with ASA Physical Status Classification I-II; those receiving elective PCNL, and participants whose preoperative chest X-ray or chest CT showed no abnormalities. The exclusion criteria were: presence of severe cardiac, hepatic, or pulmonary insufficiencies; recent history of upper respiratory tract infection; those with an abnormal coagulation function; participants whose surgery delayed for more than 24 h; those who were postoperatively transferred to ICU for treatment; subjects unable to cooperate with follow-up or poor compliance; those with loss or unavailability of crucial data, and participants who withdrew for any reason.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Lung ultrasound-guided protocolized fluid management versus conventional central venous pressure-based management in monitoring extravascular lung water during the perioperative period of percutaneous nephrolithotomy: a randomized controlled trial》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusions · S0006-p1】In conclusion, an LUS-guided fluid management protocol, integrating real-time EVLW assessment with predefined intervention thresholds, demonstrated remarkable advantages over conventional CVP-based management during the perioperative period of PCNL. The sensitivity of LUS for detecting early EVLW elevation, combined with protocolized timely intervention, helps reduce the incidence of postoperative hypoxemia, shorten extubation and patients’ PACU stay time, improve short-term perioperative recovery parameters.

【Conclusions · abstract-4-1】An LUS-guided fluid management protocol integrating real-time EVLW assessment with predefined intervention thresholds outperformed conventional CVP-based management during the perioperative period of PCNL. The superior sensitivity of LUS for detecting early EVLW elevation, combined with protocolized early intervention, reduced postoperative hypoxemia incidence, shortened extubation time and PACU stay duration, and improved short-term perioperative recovery.

【Figure 1. · F0001】Figure 1. Lung ultrasound scoring criteria. (A) When B-lines ≤ 5, the score was 0, no EVLW was observed; (B) When B-lines were 6–15, the score was 1 and mild EVLW was suggested; (C) When B-lines were 16–30, the score was 2, indicating moderate EVLW; (D) B-lines ≥31 or diffusely distributed throughout the lungs suggested severe EVLW.
